    FOI Number

    The MoD has no formal list of those UFO sightings which have been investigated.
    The list of sightings on the MoD website shows occupation for sightings from aircrew
    etc, which is probably 90% or more of investigations initiated by the MoD.

    However, it does not take into account "investigations" that were undertaken in
    answer to correspondence from the public or parliament. Therefore, the pool of files
    that must be looked at is very wide.

    Calculation

    The period 1999-09 is covered by a minimum of 19 Sighting Report files, 32
    Correspondence files, 21 Persistent Correspondent files and 4 PQ files.

    In total this is some 76 files

    To read and extract information from a single file would take a minimum of 1 hour

    76 files = 76 hours

    1 hour =f25

    76 hours x f25

    TOTAL f:l,900

    These figures exclude DIS files.

ee  no UFO report has revealed such evidence, we do not attempt to identify the precise nature of
each sighting reported to us. We believe that rational explanations, such as aircraft lights or natural
phenomena, could be found for them if resources were diverted for this purpose, but it is not the
function of the MoD to provide this kind of aerial identification service. It would be an inappropriate
use of defence resources if we were to do so.

 The MoD does not have any expertise or role in respect of ’UFOlflying saucer’ matters or the
 question of the existence or otherwise of extraterrestrial life forms, about which it remains totally
 open-minded. I should add that to date, the MoD knows of no evidence which substantiates the
 existence of these alleged phenomena.

Turning to the specifics of your request, the MoD has no files on the subject of inter governmental
communication, discussion or sharing of information on UFOs. You might wish to consider
contacting The National Archives at www.nationalarchives.gov.uk in case they have any such old
files. However, should this be the case, other UFO researchers would probably have mentioned them
by now. You may also wish to know that the MoD currently has a programme to release some 160
UFO files from the late 1970’s up to 2007 to The National Archives by the close of 2010. Files for
the period 1979-1992 have already been transferred and it is hoped those for 1992-2000 will.be
transferred by the end of the year and they will be made available for public viewing.
Alternatively, you could contact the Foreign and Commonwealth Office at www.fco.gov.uk to see if
they have any such files.
I am however, aware that there was some discussion around 1978-79 regarding a UN debate on
 UFOs and that MoD had a limited number of documents on the subject.
The MoD has no central record of UFO sightings and their proximity to military or nuclear
installations and it has been assessed that the costs for which we are permitted to charge in providing
this information will exceed the appropriate limit. This appropriate limit is specified in regulations
and for central government is set at f:600. This represents the estimated cost of one person spending
three and a half working days in determining whether the Department holds the information, and
locating, retrieving and extracting the information. Under the terms of Section 12 of the FOI Act,
this means that we are not obliged to comply with your request.
 The MOD may be able to provide information requested if you reduce or=2 Orefine your request to
 bring the cost of compliance under the limit. Please contact me if you would like to refine your
 request or require advice on doing so. In the meantime, you may be interested to know that details of
 UFO reports received by the MoD for the period 1997-2008 are available for viewing on the MoD
 website at www.mod.ukbysearchingunder..UFOReports...butincollatingthisinformation.no
 specific regard was taken of proximity to military or nuclear installations.
I hope this is helpful.
 If you are not satisfied with this response or you wish to complain about any aspect of the handling
 of your request, then you should contact me in the first instance. If informal resolution is not possible
 and you are still dissatisfied then you may apply for an independent internal review by contacting the
 Head of Corporate Information, 6th Floor, MOD Main Building, Whitehall, SWIA 2HB (e-mail
 CIO-XD@mod.uk). Please note that any request for an internal review must be made within 40
 working days of the date200n which the attempt to reach informal resolution has come to an end.
If you remain dissatisfied following an internal review, you may take your complaint to the
Information Commissioner under the provisions of Section 50 of the Freedom of Information         Act.
Please note that the Information Commissioner will not investigate your case until the MOD internal
review process has been completed. Further details of the role and powers of the Information
Commissioner can be found on the Commissioner’s website, http://www.ico.gov.uk.
